review.lane: R2 (adversarial review of the T17 change)
review.subject: Workspace-wide reference resolution in sendMany — cross-team information leak through the I4 refusal, and the skipped authorization
review.attribution: The defect is T17's: before its hunk, `validateReferences` ran against the TEAM-SCOPED slice, so a foreign question was simply `reference-unknown` (no label echo) and the answer was refused. T17 widened the reference check to `state.messages` (workspace) while leaving the ownership lookup on `scoped.messages`, which both enables the leak and skips the authorization. The cellwork dist is T18's in-flight package (cellwork inlines team-core) and is NOT charged here.

verdict.justification: The Lead's worry is REAL: a member of team X can read team Y's offered label strings out of an I4 refusal (probe 1a), the echo runs BEFORE any authorization, and with a CORRECT label the foreign answer is ACCEPTED because the ownership lookup only searches the caller's team slice (probe 1c). The same path lets a non-recipient learn a foreign thread id (probe 4a). Fix the order/scope of the checks before this lands.

probes.probe: 1 — a cross-team answer with a WRONG label (non-recipient)
probes.result: FAIL — refused as `invalid-envelope` WITH team Y's labels inline
probes.observed: detail = 'selected label is not offered by the question: "Z. made-up" (valid labels: A. secret-one, B. secret-two)'; no authorization sentence; no row written beyond Y's question.

probes.probe: 1c — a cross-team answer with a CORRECT label (non-recipient)
probes.observed: {ok:true}; a row written to the caller's own team member with answerTo = team Y's question id and threadId = team Y's thread id.

probes.probe: 2 — a question the caller IS addressed in still echoes labels
probes.observed: same-team addressee's wrong label → refusal WITH 'valid labels: A. x-one, B. x-two'.

probes.probe: 2b — same-team NON-recipient with a wrong label
probes.observed: also echoes the labels, because the echo precedes the ownership check.

sendMany order is validateEnvelope → validateReferences(workspace; performs the I4 echo) → ownership on the SCOPED byId; a foreign question is absent from the scoped map, so the ownership block is SKIPPED entirely, not merely late.

probes.result: FAIL (thread id), plus an existence oracle
probes.observed: 4a: a plain reply whose replyTo is a FOREIGN message id is accepted and the returned/stored row carries the foreign THREAD id (`threadId` = team Y's question id). 4b: a nonexistent id is refused with 'names no message', so a caller can probe which workspace ids exist.
the addressee's echo and the valid-answer path behave exactly as in R2/T7.

findings.title: Cross-team LABEL LEAK through the I4 refusal: the label echo runs before any authorization and resolves the question workspace-wide
findings.where: packages/mpd-team-core-plugin/src/mailbox-store.ts · sendMany (`validateReferences(envelope, state.messages)` before the ownership block)
findings.what: A member of team X that knows (or guesses) a team Y question id sends an answer with an invented label. `validateReferences` finds the question in the workspace fold, calls `validateAnswer(answer, target.question)`, and the I4 mismatch sentence — which inlines the FULL VALID LABEL LIST — is returned to team X. Probe 1a reproduces it exactly. The same echo also reaches a SAME-TEAM non-recipient (probe 2b), because the echo precedes the ownership check there too.
findings.why: I4's label list is a correction aid for the question's addressee. Handing it to anyone who can name a message id turns the refusal into a cross-team disclosure channel: option labels can carry the actual decision content of another wave/cell (this is precisely the data the 'no index' protocol is protecting).
findings.direction: Resolve the referenced question for the AUTHORIZATION check from the workspace fold, run the ownership check FIRST, and only then validate the echo. A non-recipient must be refused with a `not-recipient` sentence that names the question id and NOT its labels (no `labels` field, no label text). `validateReferences` should not be the thing that echoes labels on this path — split existence/reference resolution from the echo, or gate the echo behind the proven addressee.
findings.evidence: probes 1a / 2b in output.log; T17's own arm 'a cross-team answer is still refused WITH the valid label list when the echo is wrong' asserts the leak as intended

findings.title: The ownership rule is SKIPPED for a question outside the caller's team slice: a foreign answer is accepted and a foreign thread id is exposed
findings.where: packages/mpd-team-core-plugin/src/mailbox-store.ts · sendMany (`const asked = byId.get(...)` where `byId` is built from `scoped.messages`)
findings.what: When the referenced question is in another team, `asked` is undefined and the whole ownership block (only-a-recipient-may-answer; answer-goes-back-to-the-asker) is skipped instead of refusing. Probe 1c: the answer is written (ok:true) into the caller's own team with answerTo = the foreign question. The thread resolution uses the WORKSPACE map (`workspaceById`), so the written row also inherits and returns the foreign thread id (probes 1c and 4a). Probe 4b adds an existence oracle: a bogus id is refused, a foreign one is accepted.
findings.why: Contract §5's 'only a recipient of a question may answer it' must hold on the workspace-wide path; silently skipping it means team X can mint a row that claims to answer team Y's question, and the returned thread id discloses an id it could not see. The thread leak is exactly the Lead's probe 4.
findings.direction: Use the workspace fold for the ownership lookup too (`asked` from `state.messages`), so a legitimate cross-team answer (the caller IS the question's addressee) still passes while a non-recipient is refused; only then inherit the thread (or restrict inheritance to the authorized path). Keep the existence refusal generic enough that it does not distinguish owner beyond what a legitimate reply already needs.

declinedToJudge.item: The legitimate cross-team answer case T17 was written for (the answerer IS the question's addressee)
declinedToJudge.reason: The workspace-wide resolution is the right direction and its shipped arms pass; the defect is the missing authorization/ordering, not the widening itself.
T18's in-flight package (cellwork inlines team-core); pre-declared by the Lead, not charged to T17.

declinedToJudge.item: The existence oracle for a bogus id (probe 4b)
declinedToJudge.reason: An inherent consequence of workspace-wide reference checks and low value once the authorization is enforced; mentioned inside F2 rather than raised separately.
Its arms pass; the arm that asserts the label list for a cross-team wrong echo is the evidence of the leak, not a test-quality issue.

declinedToJudge.item: The backlog bound / stamps staying team-scoped
declinedToJudge.reason: Verified unchanged by T17's own arms and my probes; not the subject of this adversarial question.

Read: sendMany (the T17 hunk and the ownership/thread block), validateReferences/validateAnswer's label echo, and T17's new mail-workspace-references.test.ts arms.
Ran: 7 black-box probes over `sendMany` (cross-team wrong/valid label, same-team addressee/non-recipient, foreign reply/thread, bogus id).
